***On September 5, 2026 while extending his hand out to feed the camels at the feeding window of the camel enclosure a
man was bitten by the camel. The facility stated that it appeared the customers cuticle of one finger had been nicked
causing it to bleed. The facility failed to protect a member of the public from injury during the encounter.
During public exhibition all animals are required to be handled so there is minimal risk of harm to the animal and to the
public with sufficient distance and/or barriers between the animal and the viewing public.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the Owner.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
